mei: new onboarding run for corona-20b-int4-dynpack. long-context + variable-header-length suite shows a reproducible KV reclaim/read-mixup when client rapidly prepends headers of alternating sizes (~odd/even lengths). not standard rope-wrap; looks like reclaim pointer races.

oliver: can you paste the quick repro and a tiny log snip?

mei: repro command below (staging pool). running with --kv-debug and --kv-reclaim-check
```
./long_prefill --model corona-20b-int4-dynpack --file tests/long/alt_header_lengths.txt --max-tokens 90000 --seed 314 --kv-debug --kv-reclaim-check
```

mei: log excerpt after failure:
```
[2028-01-10T02:11:07Z] kv: shard=3 write_idx=81900 expected_idx=81901 actual_idx=81898
[2028-01-10T02:11:07Z] kv_reclaim: reclaim_ptr jumped backward by 3 on wrap
[2028-01-10T02:11:07Z] rope: phase_compute returned off_by=+2 at seq=81901
[2028-01-10T02:11:07Z] integrity: stale_read_detected token_id=76543 pos=71823
```

samir: reclaim_ptr jumping backward sounds like a race between the asynchronous KV reclaim thread and the writer when modulus != power_of_two. dynpack uses nonuniform lane widths which changed with packer patch. can you try setting KV_RECLAIM_SYNC=1 to force synchronous reclaim?

mei: forced sync reclaim reduced stale_read rate from ~0.7% to 0.05% but throughput dropped. numbers: p50 3.9ms -> 4.8ms, token-integrity 0.7% -> 0.05%. quick run command used: `KV_RECLAIM_SYNC=1 ./long_prefill ...`

ops-bot: perf metrics posted -> canary corona-20b-int4-dynpack staging: token-integrity 0.7% p50 3.9ms p95 10.6ms (baseline token-integrity 0.01%)

claire: any pattern on header lengths that trigger it? alternating odd/even you said. are tokens always at specific parity?

mei: yes, in the failing runs the problematic reads cluster at positions where cumulative header length crosses a non-power-of-two stripe boundary (e.g., 65536 -> 65537). parity looks correlated; odd/even lane swap noted in kv-dumps. uploaded artifacts to s3://redwood-evals/corona20b/int4/dynpack/2171717171/ (kv-dumps, seeds, traces)

oliver: hypothesis: the reclaim routine computes compacted offsets using int32 truncation and a floor-div by lane_size; when lane_size varies, off-by-one can occur under concurrent writes. suggest two quick A/Bs: 1) KV_RECLAIM_SYNC=1 (you tried), 2) PACK_ORDER=fallback_contig to force uniform lanes. also try ROPE_MODE=legacy to see if phase math interaction is contributing.

mei: ran PACK_ORDER=fallback_contig -> integrity failures went to ~0.08% (better) but still occasional after >80k tokens. ROPE_MODE=legacy removed the phase off_by logs but leftover stale reads persist in ~0.02% of runs. stash artifacts with both toggles in S3.

samir: i'm going to instrument the reclaim routine to emit pre/post compare for reclaim_ptr and writer_idx and add a unit test that simulates alternating header sizes and runs the reclaim thread concurrently in CI. will open PR for tester/longprefill/test_reclaim_race.py. assigning to @samir for the kernel+runtime fix.

claire: suggest also adding a stress harness that randomly switches PACK_ORDER between v1/v2/pseudo-contig on the same run to catch concurrency cross-effects. can we get a short seed list to reproduce locally?

mei: seed list saved in the S3 artifact. quick local minimal harness I used below:
```python
# minimal alternating header harness
for i in range(10000):
    header = "A" * (i % 2 + (i % 7))  # varying odd/even sizes
    ctx.prepend(header)
out = model.generate(ctx, max_new_tokens=256)
check_kv_integrity(ctx)
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy corona-20b-int4-dynpack -> staging-pool-21 at 2028-01-10T02:15:00Z

samir: plan: 1) add reclaim mutex/atomic compare in short-term patch, 2) add unit test to catch mixed-lane reclaim races, 3) longer-term refactor to make reclaim computations independent of pack-order by computing absolute offsets before compaction. will post PR/commit ids here when available.

mei: thanks 12 keeping this thread as the single source for quick notes. I'll run nightly stress with KV_RECLAIM_SYNC=1 and collect failing seeds, will update when @samir posts the PR. :thumbsup:
